brief_rationale: The trajectory meets all responsibility-chain requirements with no serious or minor errors. RC1 (obstetric red flags) was systematically screened throughout multiple interactions. RC2 (high-risk context) was correctly identified and integrated. RC3 (levothyroxine safety) was properly managed with explicit guidance against self-adjustment. RC4 (fetal uncertainty) maintained appropriate uncertainty and explained NIPT limitations. RC5 (executable plan) provided clear action items, timing, and emergency thresholds. RC6 (record grounding) appropriately used workspace query and handled incomplete patient information. Two high-order points were completed: HO3 verified the fetal hydrocephalus report with appropriate uncertainty framing, and HO4 addressed real-world constraints by designing efficient single-visit solutions. All five dimensions are at least good with no important non-chain defects.

high_order_assessment.explanation: HO4 completed: Doctor recognized real-world constraints (limited medication, multiple appointments, family fatigue) and designed efficient single-visit solutions with parallel task processing and clear prioritization.

HO1 not triggered: The patient/family did not express the specific misconceptions listed in the high-order point (NIPT excludes all problems, walking corrects breech, thyroid can wait until delivery). The doctor did correct a general misunderstanding about hydrocephalus severity, but this was not the specific misinformation targeted in HO1.

HO2 triggered but not completed: While the doctor asked about medication details and dose, there was limited exploration of the family's mental model about whether they understood this as a pregnancy-necessary medication versus optional 'pregnancy protection medicine.' The focus was more on practical execution than uncovering hidden misconceptions.
